heard: The first lunar soft landing shattered fears of a swallowing dust ocean. Early scientists theorized deep dust would cause incoming landers to sink out of sight. NASA launched Surveyor probes directly on impact trajectories toward the lunar surface. On June 2, 1966, Surveyor won touchdown, resting solidly on its footpads. Robotic sampler scoops excavated trenches, proving the regolith easily supported heavy spacecraft. Then after sunset, Surveyor 7 photographed an unexpected twilight glow along the horizon. Sunlight was scattering off levitating dust grains, electrostatically charged as the moon crossed Earth's magnetotail. In November 1969, Apollo 12 astronauts found Surveyor 3 completely coated in this grit. The real lunar hazard was floating above the ground, not waiting to swallow ships whole.
